gen-gf-warnes-work-sans: Stretched ink, bold and loose. Work Sans follows with a high mean line and open curve tips, giving Warnes plenty of room to stand out on the page.
gen-irish-grover-poppins: Poppins draws rope-loose curves at the same heft as its stems, with no thick-thin flicker. And Irish Grover matches that sturdiness with tall, chunky lowercase and softly varied strokes, so both feel big-boned.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-asap: Gugi throws neon-tube strokes and tall lowercase that nearly touch the capitals, with terminals cut open for flow. Asap simply reads easily.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-amulya: Single-nib swagger, then a quiet follow-up. And Amulya's generous curve gaps give Gabarito's flat, unmodulated lines something relaxed to sit against.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-chillax: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its terminals cut open so every counter flows outward, while Chillax loosens into spaghetti lines. Their strongest trait is playfulness.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-plein: Expressive from the first letter, Gabarito has diagonals that match its stems exactly. But Plein feels reliable beside it, with a clear channel leading into each round shape.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-spline-sans: Nib-drawn and open-ended, Gabarito sets a lively tone with terminals cut so each counter flows outward and nothing feels pinched. Spline Sans is approachable and wide.
gen-gf-gabarito-fs-synonym: Gabarito arrives with a one-nib look and terminals cut open, letting its counters flow outward in a distinctive way. Synonym keeps a plain stripe of ink beneath it.
gen-gf-gabarito-outfit: Distinctive, with a nib-drawn lead. Outfit's cable-like curves stop short of closing and never swell or thin, so paragraphs of text feel smooth and airy.
gen-gf-gabarito-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans is precise and monoline, its curve endings kept well apart. Gabarito, meanwhile, does the expressive work, with a nib-drawn look and open terminals, while Plus Jakarta Sans handles the quiet, exact text.
